Spider Solitaire · Objective-C → Unity port

iPhone 7 — Unity Port Fidelity

Unity 8.0.0  vs  Obj-C 7.42.5  ·  750×1334  ·  15 screens  ·  build 337

Build 337 clears the earlier content bugs — the FAQ now loads Spider’s own content, the main-menu promo-icon strip is back, the difficulty smiley cursor returns, and the victory buttons are red again. It is still not pixel-faithful though: two bugs remain — the FAQ duplicates its first question and a “Dev Panel” debug button ships on both win screens — plus systemic typography drift and dropped ad banners. Drag any image to wipe between the builds; switch to Diff for the exact changed pixels (red).

Findings · triage

Grouped for the porting team, most actionable first.

  • Content bug
    FAQ duplicates its first questionFAQ

    The FAQ now shows Spider’s own content (build 335’s “wrong game” Klondike text is fixed), but the first entry — “How do I play the game?” — renders twice, back-to-back, identical.

  • Content bug
    “Dev Panel” debug button ships on the win screensVictory

    Both victory screens show a “Dev Panel” button at the bottom-right — a development-only control that should not be present in a shipping build.

  • Layout drift
    Typography & content deltassystemic

    Unity renders body text heavier and wraps it differently, so text shifts even where the words match — the main driver of the Help / Options / FAQ / More Games diffs. Also: lowercase “options” title; More Games lists extra titles; Stats markers “*” vs “✻” with lowercase headers; Game Table / In-Game Menu drop the bottom ad banner.

  • Correct
    Fixed since build 335regression check

    Several earlier defects are resolved: the FAQ loads Spider’s own content (was the wrong game’s); the main-menu promo-icon strip is back; Difficulty’s smiley cursor returns and its stray entries are gone; the victory buttons are red again and Victory · Score no longer shows a promo strip.

  • Correct
    Still correctAbout · Help · Cards

    About keeps its “▷” divider and correct “submit feedback”; Help shows a single “Introduction”; Choose Look · Cards reads “symbols”; the Choose-Look modal is well-positioned.
